claim: United Airlines operates roughly 68% of flights at Washington Dulles; Delta, the next-largest carrier, operates about 4%, making IAD a single-carrier hub.
source_title: Washington Dulles' 5 Largest Airlines By Market Share
supporting_excerpt: United operates 68% of the flights at the airport, with Delta Air Lines a very distant second at just 4%.
caveat: Share of flights, not seats or enplanements; secondary source. Confirm against MWAA air traffic statistics.

claim: Washington Dulles handled a record 27.25 million passengers in 2024, exceeding the prior 2005 record.
source_title: Dulles Airport's 2024 passenger total set new all-time record
supporting_excerpt: just over 27.25 million passengers traveled through the airport in 2024, representing a new all-time record set in 2024, topping the previous all-time record set in 2005.
caveat: Total passengers, not enplanements; confirm against MWAA CAFR.

claim: Dulles cost per enplanement peaked at $26.55 in 2014, a level United found unmanageable, and was later reduced to about $17 via a new airline agreement and a $50 million Virginia grant.
source_title: This Washington DC Airport Set Not 1, But 2 New Records In 2024
supporting_excerpt: the authority lowered the cost per enplanement to $17 per passenger from a peak of $26.55 in 2014... a new agreement with airlines and later a $50 million grant from Virginia.
airport_or_entity: IAD / United Airlines / MWAA / Commonwealth of Virginia
caveat: Secondary press; exact CPE figures and the $50M grant terms should be verified in MWAA financial statements and the airline use-and-lease agreement.

claim: United cut seats at Dulles by nearly 18% from 2010 to 2015 as costs and disproportionate debt service rose, before MWAA cost relief reversed the decline.
source_title: This Washington DC Airport Set Not 1, But 2 New Records In 2024
supporting_excerpt: United cut seats at Dulles by nearly 18% from 2010 to 2015... The hub was bearing disproportionate debt service... the cost per enplanement (CPE) had reached a peak of $26.55 in 2014.
caveat: Secondary source; seat-count basis and exact percentage should be confirmed against Diio/OAG or DOT schedule data.

claim: Washington Dulles is repeatedly ranked the most expensive major US airport by average domestic fare, roughly $475-$490 in 2025.
source_title: Washington Dulles found to be most expensive US airport at $475, according to new study
supporting_excerpt: Washington Dulles International Airport ranked as the most expensive major airport in the U.S., with travelers forking over an average domestic airfare of about $475 in early 2025.
caveat: Average fare is a passenger price metric, NOT airline CPE; use only as a proxy for IAD cost reputation. Based on a third-party study, not primary DOT data.

claim: RWY 1L/19R at Dulles is the fourth runway, 9,400 feet, opened in 2008 - the runway whose approach/departure surfaces the proposed data center would occupy.
source_title: FAA Reviewing Washington Dulles' Longstanding Plan To Construct 5th Runway
supporting_excerpt: Fourth Runway (Completed 2008) - Designation: Runway 1L/19R - Length: 9,400 feet - Opening: 2008.
caveat: Runway designation and length should be cross-checked against the FAA airport diagram and MWAA ALP.

claim: The Dulles fifth runway has been planned since the 1950s, was in the 1985 master plan, was FAA-approved alongside the fourth runway in the mid-2000s, and was reaffirmed by the MWAA Board on July 16, 2025 as part of a build-out toward ~90 million annual passengers by the 2080s-2090s.
source_title: Dulles Master Plan Update Sets Framework for Decades of Airport Development
supporting_excerpt: the updated plan... includes provisions for a fifth runway... The plan aims to increase capacity toward 90 million annual passengers by 2080-2090.
caveat: Board approval date and passenger horizon from MWAA release; fifth-runway FAA Record of Decision date corroborated by secondary sources (mid-2000s alongside fourth runway).

claim: United is expanding at Dulles again after the cost relief: Concourse E is being built specifically for United (opening late 2026) and United added roughly 10 new routes in 2024.
source_title: Dulles Airport Got A United Airlines Hub. Now It Wants More Cargo.
supporting_excerpt: United is the dominant carrier at the airport... In 2024 specifically, 10 new routes were added from United Airlines; Concourse E is being built specifically for United.
caveat: Route count from press; Concourse E purpose and timing widely reported. Confirm route count against schedule data.

claim: Northern Virginia data centers generate very large non-aeronautical-style revenue: Loudoun County data centers fund roughly one-third of the county's $3 billion budget, illustrating the revenue temptation behind an airport data-center lease.
source_title: Loudoun County, Virginia: The Heart of the Data-Center Boom
supporting_excerpt: Tax revenue from data centers now accounts for nearly a third of Loudoun County's $3 billion budget.
caveat: County tax revenue, not an airport ground-lease figure; used to establish scale of the counter-case, not as a projection of IAD lease value.

claim: Dominion Energy's transmission into Loudoun is already constrained (PJM flagged an emergency build-out in 2022), which raises the likelihood of on-site/behind-the-meter power generation at new data centers and the associated thermal plume near the airfield.
source_title: Energy demands for Northern Virginia data centers almost too big to compute
supporting_excerpt: In summer 2022, Dominion Energy found it lacked enough transmission lines and substations for the growing number of data centers in Loudoun County. Consequently, PJM advised an emergency construction program.
airport_or_entity: Loudoun County / Dominion Energy (context for IAD)
caveat: Establishes plausibility of on-site generation risk; does not confirm the specific IAD project would use on-site generation.
